tools.semgrep: 1.178.0, config p/default (CI artifact for main, local run after fixes)
tools.pip-audit: backend runtime dependencies from uv export (40 packages)

findings.title: Actions referenced by mutable tags
findings.rationale: A tag can be repointed by the action owner. All actions are now pinned to a full commit SHA with the version in a comment, as the deploy workflows already were.

findings.title: Reusable deploy workflow receives every secret
findings.rationale: deploy.yml now declares the five secrets it uses and the callers pass them by name. GitHub requires passing environment secrets explicitly, so deploy-dev must be checked after merge.

findings.title: No dependency cooldown for uv
findings.rationale: exclude-newer = "7 days" added. Relocking moved markupsafe 3.0.3 to 3.0.4, sqlalchemy 2.1.2 to 2.1.3 and tzdata 2026.4 to 2026.5, all older than 7 days; the backend suite passes.

findings.title: Bun minimum release age is 24 hours, not 7 days
findings.rationale: bunfig.toml is used only by Lovable's bun install. CI and the frontend image install with npm ci from package-lock.json. The Lovable-managed file already has a 24-hour guard; 7 days would block packages Lovable adds. Revisit if bun becomes part of CI.

findings.title: add_header in a location block
findings.rationale: The server block sets no headers, so nothing is overwritten. The only add_header (Cache-Control for hashed assets) is the intended one.

findings.title: urllib with a non-literal URL
findings.rationale: select_cuad.py opens the constant CUAD_ZIP_URL. smoke.py builds the URL from the backend URL its operator passes on the command line. No user input reaches either, and both are local or CI tools, not part of the app.

findings.title: Bracketed tokens in the contract make findings disappear
findings.rationale: Real correctness and manipulation risk: template tokens like [CLIENT_NAME] or a hostile [REF_1] drop correct findings silently. Register existing bracket tokens as identity mappings; add a test and an eval case.

findings.title: No per-user cap on analyses; the shared quota and threadpool can be exhausted
findings.rationale: Open registration plus a shared 200K tokens/day Groq quota: one user can block analyses for everyone. Cap analyses in flight per user and per day; a dedicated executor is deferred to the next phase.

findings.title: Contract text is not framed as untrusted data
findings.rationale: The counterparty writes the contract, so prompt injection is in scope. Frame the contract as untrusted data with delimiters and add injection cases to the eval. Done after the prompt v4 decision to keep the eval comparable.

findings.title: One overlong field fails the whole analysis
findings.rationale: Validate findings one by one after restore and drop invalid ones with a logged reason, as with quote_not_found.

findings.title: Superseded or stale runs keep calling Groq
findings.rationale: Wastes tokens only under queueing; MR-2 removes most of the cause. Revisit with the worker queue.

findings.title: Validation errors logged contract text
findings.rationale: Already fixed in cccdeb7 (hide_input_in_errors on all models), before this audit.

findings.title: main has no branch protection or ruleset
findings.rationale: The one-PR-per-step rule and green CI before merge exist only as a convention in AGENTS.md; anyone with a token, including a coding agent, can push to main and trigger deploy-dev. Add a ruleset: pull request required, CI checks required, no force push.

findings.title: The local coding agent runs with the developer's AWS and GitHub credentials
findings.rationale: Claude Code runs in the developer's shell, where the AWS CLI is configured for an IAM user and gh is logged in. Today only permission prompts stand between the agent and those credentials. Deny aws and gh merge/secret commands in the project permissions and document it (agent extension pack).
